strengths: Addresses practically relevant tall data setting in SBI where multiple observations are available

weaknesses: Limited novelty: core contribution is straightforward application of Bayes rule to combine individual observation scores; heavily relies on existing Gaussian approximation results (Boys et al., 2023)

Weak theoretical justification: Gaussian approximations of backward kernels (Eq. 9-10) lack rigorous justification; no error bounds or convergence guarantees provided; circular reasoning in setting F(θ,x₁:ₙ) = 0 by construction

Experimental instability and questionable practices: (a) outlier removal of up to 3% of results; (b) ad-hoc sample clipping to (-3,3) to stabilize JAC and LANGEVIN, introducing bias; (c) unexplained MMD growth with n on SBI benchmarks (Figures 12-13), contradicting the motivation
JAC algorithm is practically unusable: extreme instability with any score perturbation (Figure 2), requires analytical scores, ~2× slower than GAUSS, and only works when ε = 0

Growing MMD with multiple observations: Figures 12-13 show approximation error accumulates with more observations, undermining the tall data advantage; partial factorization (Appendix K) suggested as fix but represents significant methodological retreat

Uncertain advantages over F-NPSE: comparison potentially unfair (F-NPSE hyperparameters appear untuned); 'equivalent time setting' is arbitrary; Appendix J shows alternative Langevin variants can be more stable

Score model dependency: method still requires careful training of single-observation score model; performance heavily dependent on Ntrain (Figure 3); doesn't solve fundamental score estimation problem

Missing theoretical analysis: no convergence rates, error bounds, or analysis of error accumulation with n; positive definiteness conditions unclear; no characterization of when Gaussian approximation is valid
Σ₀ estimation in GAUSS uses only 100 DDIM iterations with no sensitivity analysis or justification for sufficiency
Limited experimental scope: moderate dimensions only (m ≤ 5 for benchmarks); single neuroscience application; unclear generalizability

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: toy models with ground truth → SBI benchmarks → neuroscience application, with proper controls isolating sampling from score quality effects
